chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a slain person is found in an open wasteland, his blood-money is to be paid from the Bayt al-Mal, for Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say: “The blood of a Muslim man must not be left uncompensated.”

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.بَيْتِ الْمَالِ: the public treasury of the Muslim polity
key_terms.دَمُ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ: the life-blood of a Muslim person, whose right must be protected
key_terms.فَلَاةٍ: an open desert or uninhabited wasteland
key_terms.قَتِيلٌ: a slain person or murder victim

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a murdered Muslim is found in a deserted place and the killer is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a slain person found in a deserted land when the killer is unknown. In such a case, the diyah is paid from the Bayt al-Mal, reflecting the principle stated by Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام that the blood of a Muslim must not be allowed to go in vain.
